outline.chapter_title: 1 | Motivation and Challenges in Controlling Language Models
outline.description:
"Large language models" learnt horizons mainly through massive unsupervised corpora display surprising breadth of knowledge yet lack precise steerability towards desired behaviours such as safety tags or sentiment biasing.

To build dependable AI systems it is essential to select among their diverse capabilities according to human intent.
The first few sections introduce these practical needs, survey prior alignment activities online academical contexts,
and point surgical limitations inherent when relying solely on unconstrained generation.

outline.chapter_title: 2 | Background – From Unsupervised LMs to Preference Models
outline.description:
"Supervised Fine‑Tuning", “SFT”, grounds most PRIMITIVE alignment systems.
It curates demonstrations before humans supply relative quality feedback.
Key concepts introduced are:
 * Explicit architectures (transformer decoder).
 * SFT workflow leading straight into downstream prompts.
 * Generation pipelines embed tactic dialogues , summaries , creative hugging deep.
 * The classical reinforcement learning pathway featuring (i.) reward modelling through Bradley‑Terry logic;
and (ii.) solving an optimisation problem over expected reward minus KL divergence.

"Relative judgments" rather than absolute scores simplify data collection.
To map these judgments into trainable components a probabilistic choice rule such as Bradley–Terry describes probability that one response wins over another.
Key technical points:
 * Logistic link versus linear score representation.
 * Parameter evoked patterns (‘reward’ surfaces).
 * Requirement that rewards have zero mean per prompt mitigates underdetermination.
 * Extension towards Plackett–Luce handles multi‑way rankings.
subtopics: "Maximum likelihood estimation gives an easy negative hash loss"

outline.chapter_title: "4 | Reinforcement Learning With KL Constraint In Language Generation'
outline.description:
'Reward measure' influences generate language but must not diverge too far from its base distribution.
Formulating an objective `Μ[Y←πθ]rφ − β·KL[πθ‖πref]` yields an analytically tractable optimal policy:
fixed ratio between πadv and πref weighted proportionally to exp(rβ⁻¹).
Mathematical elements clarified:
 • Closed form expression derived substitution path.
 • Partition‐function makes direct evaluation unrealistic given discrete EOS sequences.
 • β controls exploitation versus safety -- becomes Lagrange multiplier.

[DPO] converts “reward → policy” loop into “policy → loss” rule
by reexpressing r(x,y)=β·log[πnew/πref]+constant.
After inserting this expression into Bradley Terry’s pairwise probability it eliminates Z(x)
and delivers an elegant cross‑entropy trade barion:
always reduces classification error without recurrent sampling stages
or explicit Reward Model training.
